text.insert: The prompt-kit connection exposes ten tools over MCP stdio. An authenticated loopback service owns task snapshots while prompt files remain authoritative across service restarts.

fields.name: project
fields.description: Use the explicit project ID returned by discovery.

fields.name: prompt_id
fields.description: Use the discovered prompt identity, which can differ from the agent name.

fields.name: task_id
fields.description: Scopes writes to the workspace, project, profile, and knowledge snapshot.

fields.name: expected_hash
fields.description: Current pk1 revision returned by reading the prompt.

fields.name: ops
fields.description: One ordered batch applied to a scratch document before persistence.

operations.name: prompts_discover
operations.description: Scans explicit roots and bounded workspace members. Reports malformed entries without importing executable context or starting a Kernel. With project, returns only that project's prompts and errors, and refuses a project outside the workspace.

params.name: workspace
params.description: Absolute workspace path. Defaults to the connected workspace.

params.name: project
params.description: A project ID from this workspace. Limits the result to that project's prompts and discovery errors.

operations.name: prompts_begin
operations.description: Pins the profile and the guidance snapshot, and returns task_id, profile, snapshot_id, and project. It returns no guidance text.

operations.name: prompts_guidance
operations.description: With task_id, reads the task snapshot and records the topic part as read. Without a task, loads current guidance. Without topic, lists the topics with sizes, parts, and required_for.

params.name: topic
params.type: standards | workflow | operations | work-requests | catalog | editor

params.name: part
params.description: The part of a topic over 24,576 bytes, from 1.

operations.name: prompts_capabilities
operations.description: Returns the capabilities index in pages of at most 4,096 bytes. It holds versions, the guidance snapshot, the tool order, and each topic with its size and required_for. It also names prompts_discover with the prompt count and lists the project IDs.

operations.name: prompts_read
operations.description: Returns normalized document, production render, address map, hash, declarations, and findings without saving.

operations.name: prompts_apply_ops
operations.description: Saves a valid operation batch immediately and returns the canonical document, render, revision, and durable changeId. Refuses until the task reads every part of topic standards.
operations.exampleCall: prompts_apply_ops({ project: "example-0641b415", prompt_id: "rewritePrompt", task_id: "2d493d1e-0271-4c1f-8ee7-0c95c50814b9", expected_hash: "pk1-7e8f94a2e9a1517a46c53f412a9940b1ce5eff2a09153e8acf58a72fd6a558ab", ops: [{ op: "update_node", nodeId: "opening", patch: { content: ["Rewrite the paragraph in two sentences."] } }] })

operations.name: prompts_undo
operations.description: Requires the recorded resulting revision to remain current and revalidates the restored document against current declarations.
operations.exampleCall: prompts_undo({ project: "example-0641b415", prompt_id: "rewritePrompt", task_id: "2d493d1e-0271-4c1f-8ee7-0c95c50814b9", expected_hash: "pk1-<saved revision>", change_id: "<changeId from the save>" })

operations.name: prompts_check
operations.description: Checks structure, variables, and profile rules at the current revision. With task_id, it also rereads each changed prompt and reports missing or outdated successful checks.

params.name: task_id
params.description: Supply to record completion against the task and to add the task report.

fields.name: snapshot_id
fields.description: With task_id: the task's pinned snapshot.

fields.name: changed
fields.description: With task_id: each prompt the task changed, its current hash, and whether that revision passed.

fields.name: all_current_revisions_checked
fields.description: With task_id: true when every changed prompt passed at its current hash.

operations.name: prompts_requests
operations.description: Lists the open agent requests on one prompt and the annotations hash to pass as expected_hash.

operations.name: prompts_request_reply
operations.description: Without close, adds body as a reply and leaves the request open. With close true, resolves the request with body as its one-sentence resolution.

params.name: close
params.description: true closes the request with body as its resolution.

operations.exampleCall: prompts_request_reply({ project: "example-0641b415", prompt_id: "rewritePrompt", task_id: "2d493d1e-0271-4c1f-8ee7-0c95c50814b9", request_id: "<id from prompts_requests>", expected_hash: "<hash from prompts_requests>", body: "Cut the intro to two sentences.", close: true })

text.insert: Every mutation requires a task in the same workspace and project plus a current prompt hash. prompts

ops also requires that the task read every part of topic standards. Guidance is pinned within a task, and new tasks observe updated canonical standards. A task expires 30 minutes after its last call or 12 hours after prompts_begin.

Catalog declarations come from agent manifests. Standalone prompts must explicitly declare variables; an empty array means none. Unknown declarations permit reads but block mutation and successful checks. The store reloads declarations inside the prompt lock.

Structural errors and undeclared variables block persistence. Selected-profile findings are returned after saves and must be resolved for completion. Generic profile does not impose agent section order. A successful check establishes deterministic validity, not behavioral quality.
A task provides stable knowledge while the revision guard protects shared data. Neither task lifetime nor client identity gives exclusive ownership of a prompt.
